verdict.rationale: The only relevant evidence is community comments. One confirms Google's own 'sync to local' desktop software exists on Mac but calls it unreliable, noting synced 'files' are often just URLs whose content isn't downloaded. Another implies desktop clients exist for non-Linux platforms. There is no first-party documentation of the desktop client, so this isn't a vendor claim being contradicted, but the capability is only thinly and negatively evidenced. Missing for 10: official docs for desktop clients on macOS and Windows, a Windows client explicitly evidenced, selective sync, on-demand/online-only file support, and positive hands-on corroboration of sync reliability.
